newsitem.title: USA: Proler sues joint venture partner Hugo Neu.
newsitem.headline: Proler sues joint venture partner Hugo Neu.

text.p: Proler International Corp. said Thursday it has begun litigation against Hugo Neu Corp., its joint venture partner in the scrap metals business, for trying to block the company's proposed merger with Schnitzer Steel Industries Inc.
Separately, Hugo Neu said it obtained a temporary restraining order in New York State Supreme Court on Tuesday prohibiting Proler from disclosing confidential business information to Schnitzer.
Houston-based Proler, which recycles scrap metals and industrial wastes to produce commercial products, agreed earlier this month to be acquired by Schnitzer for $7.50 a share, or about $35 million.
At the time, Proler said it had rejected an offer from Hugo Neu to buy its interests in the companies' three scrap metals joint ventures.
Proler said it initiated litigation in Harris County, Texas, after learning of Hugo Neu's temporary restraining order, which it said appears to undermine its merger agreement with Schnitzer.
Proler is seeking compensatory and punitive damages for any resulting losses that may be incurred by the company and its stockholders.
Hugo Neu said it considers Schnitzer a competitor of its scrap metal business with Proler and that a hearing has been scheduled for Oct. 2 to look at its request for an injunction.
Proler's stock fell 12.5 cents to $7.25 on the New York Stock Exchange at mid-morning. Schnitzer was unchanged at $28.25 on Nasdaq.
